{{Use American English|date = March 2019}}
{{short description|Generalization of Vandermonde's identity}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Rothe–Hagen identity''' is a [[mathematical identity]] valid for all [[complex number]]s (<math>x, y, z</math>) except where its denominators [[Zero of a function|vanish]]:

:<math>\sum_{k=0}^n\frac{x}{x+kz}{x+kz \choose k}\frac{y}{y+(n-k)z}{y+(n-k)z \choose n-k}=\frac{x+y}{x+y+nz}{x+y+nz \choose n}.</math>

It is a generalization of [[Vandermonde's identity]], and is named after the independent work of [[Heinrich August Rothe]] in 1793 and of [[Johann Georg Hagen]] in 1891.
